title: Extended Post-Operative Oral Tranexamic Acid Dosing After ACL Reconstruction
official: Extended Post-Operative Oral Tranexamic Acid Dosing After ACL Reconstruction: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial (SM25091)
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether taking oral tranexamic acid (TXA) for one week after anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction improves recovery in adolescents and young adults aged 14 to 25 years. All participants receive standard intravenous TXA during surgery. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does oral TXA lower knee pain at 2 weeks after surgery?
* Does oral TXA reduce the amount of opioid pain medicine used in the first 2 weeks?
* Does oral TXA improve knee range of motion at 2 weeks?

Researchers will compare oral TXA to a placebo (a look-alike capsule with no active drug) to see if oral TXA improves pain, opioid use, motion, strength, knee function, and return to sport.

Participants will:

* Take 3 capsules (oral TXA or placebo) once a day for the first 8 days after surgery (day of surgery through day 7)
* Keep a home diary for 2 weeks recording pain scores, opioid pills taken and any side effects
* Return for study visits at 2 weeks, 6 weeks, 12 weeks, 6 months, 9 months and 1 year for pain, motion, strength and function testing
* Complete a survey at 2 years
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 14 to 25 years with an ACL tear undergoing primary ACL reconstruction with bone-patellar tendon-bone autograft
* Closed or closing proximal tibial and distal femoral physes on preoperative imaging (less than 1 year of growth remaining by MRI and radiographic bone age)
* Weight of at least 100 lbs (45.4 kg)
* Fluent in English

Exclusion Criteria:

* Revision ACL reconstruction, multiligament knee reconstruction, or concurrent lateral extra-articular tenodesis or anterolateral ligament reconstruction
* Concomitant meniscal repair or cartilage procedure requiring non-weightbearing or partial weightbearing after surgery (confirmed at the end of surgery, before randomization)
* History of deep vein thrombosis or other thromboembolic event
* History of renal impairment
* History of seizure
* Pregnant or breastfeeding
* Known allergy or hypersensitivity to tranexamic acid
* Use of combination hormonal contraception, tissue plasminogen activators, Factor IX complex or anti-inhibitor coagulant concentrates, or all-trans retinoic acid
